An automated Python pipeline driven by Claude and TTS now compiles offline-ready HTML materials with embedded screenshots, synchronized voiceovers and bilingual support in under 30 minutes. Challenge High manual overhead: structuring text, translating multi-step guides, logging video timestamps and aligning voiceovers took hours per lecture. Technical fragmentation: browsers can’t switch between audio tracks inside a single video, which complicates localized training. Solution Three-step pipeline: code parses .docx files and video keyframes, Claude analyzes visuals, drafts instructions and translates, then everything is compiled locally. Robust media sync with decoupled audio tracks and smart pause logic, so visuals align without speed distortion. A portable, self-contained package (236 MB) running on local Python and FFmpeg. Impact Production time for a 3-language multimedia guide dropped from 5+ hours to 20–30 minutes. Asset embedding, translation and audio clipping are fully automated and can run in the background. d: Welcome to the Pumpkin-Heads family.
x: art portfolio Welcome Pumpkin-Heads family On the edge of a misty forest, where summer meets eternal twilight, lives the Pumpkinhead family. They weren’t born; they grew from seeds of ancient magic and a sincere love for Halloween. The elders make sure the candles inside never go out, for that inner glow is their very soul. They are the guardians of coziness during the coldest season. When November comes, they don’t vanish but simply fall asleep beneath the leaves, dreaming of ripe berries and autumn rains, waiting for their time to grace your postcards once again.

d: How pigeonpolly.com handles your data.
x: privacy Privacy Short and honest: what this site keeps about you, why, and how to get it deleted. Last updated: 8 October 2026. Who is responsible Alina Otkinska (Pigeon Polly Art Lab), Riga, Latvia. You can reach me through the Write to me form. Just visiting The site is hosted by Cloudflare . It counts visits with Cloudflare Web Analytics, which uses no cookies and builds no personal profiles. Cloudflare may keep short technical logs (like IP addresses) for security. On the Daily Challenge page, the photo you add for a share card stays in your browser and is never uploaded. Your settings (level, black & white mode) are saved only in your browser. Forms When you use Write to me , your message and e-mail are delivered to my inbox through FormSubmit . I use them only to reply, and delete them on request. Your account (sign-in on any page) You sign in with Google . From Google I receive your Google account ID and e-mail address. I store: your Google account ID and e-mail, only to sign you in (never shown to anyone); your nickname (required: you choose it right after your first sign-in), the sketches you upload, their dates and themes; the time of your last visit (rounded to about 10 minutes), to show recent visitors in the flock on the home page; your consent to show sketches publicly; one sign-in cookie ( pp_s ) that keeps you logged in for up to 180 days. Public, visible to everyone on the site: your nickname and your profile with sketches, streak, level and badges; your pixel bird (or cat, or crow) with your nickname in the flock on the home page; your nickname next to your blog comments. Private: your e-mail and the time of your last visit. By signing in you agree that your nickname is public, so please don’t use your real full name if you don’t want to. Why I may do this: to provide the service you asked for, including the public nickname and the flock (GDPR Art. 6(1)(b)) and, for showing your sketches publicly, your consent (Art. 6(1)(a)). You can withdraw it at any time by deleting a sketch or your whole account. How long: your sketches stay while you are active. If you neither upload anything nor visit the site for more than 3 months, your sketches may be deleted automatically, but only when the storage is almost full (oldest inactivity first); your nickname, best streak and badges stay so you can come back. Your account stays until you delete it. Deleting the account removes all your data right away. You must be at least 13 years old to create an account. Blog: likes and comments To remember your like and give you an anonymous name in comments (like “Robin 47”), the blog sets a random browser ID in a cookie ( pp_a , up to 400 days). It contains nothing about you. When you comment, I store the comment text, the date and, if you are signed in, your Challenge nickname. To stop spam, I also store a scrambled code (hash) made from your IP address; the address itself is not saved. Comments with links are checked by me before they appear. You can ask me to delete your comment at any time. Book news by e-mail If you leave your e-mail under a book with “Get an email when the book is out”, I store only the address , the site language, the date and the text you agreed to. I use it for one thing: to write to you when the book is published. I send these e-mails myself, with all addresses hidden (BCC), and I don’t share the list with anyone. Why I may do this: your consent (GDPR Art. 6(1)(a)). How long: until the book is out and the news is sent, or until you unsubscribe — with the “Unsubscribe” link under the book or by simply replying to my e-mail. The address is then deleted right away. Cookies Only the sign-in cookie above (and the blog cookie pp_a ), and only after you sign in or use the blog. It is strictly necessary, so there is no cookie banner. d: Wobbleland: an island of eleven towns drawn in pixels. Explore the interactive map and meet every town with Polly as your guide.
x: an illustrated island Welcome to Wobbleland! Greetings, dear reader. My name is Polly, and I am a pigeon. Though, to be entirely precise, I am not quite an ordinary representative of my species. I suppose in our world, no one is surprised by a bird capable of holding a conversation over a cup of strong morning coffee or critically reviewing the latest literary releases with a look on her face, if, of course, a pigeon can be said to have a face. My life, much like the life of Wobbleland itself, is a sequence of small oddities that have become second nature. But if you do not mind the company of a feathered guide with a sharp beak and an even sharper eye for things, I shall be your guide. After all, who else is going to tell you about our island the way a bird would, one who is accustomed to seeing everything from the height of a ledge and knows a little more about city secrets than any self-respecting townsperson ought to? — Polly, your feathered guide 🗺 Explore the map 📖 Recipe book 📅 Holiday calendar Polly’s Recipe Book Ripple Tickle Sea Eleven towns, one wobble Tap a crest on the map, or a town below, to open its page.
